generator_view.scenario: An outdoor worker needs a phone setup for full shifts at temperatures down to minus 15 degrees Celsius. Their current phone can show about 40 percent charge and then shut down suddenly in the cold. They are comparing an OUKITEL WP9 rugged phone, a LATIMERIA 26800 mAh solar power bank, a TG90 6000 mAh wired power bank, and a JUBOTY 7000 mAh battery case. They care more about verified cold-shift endurance and compatibility than printed capacity, ruggedness, or runtime claims, and they can keep the phone and backup power together in an insulated inner pouch and run a representative cold-load test before relying on a setup at work.
generator_view.target: Explain why a phone can shut down in the cold while still displaying substantial charge; audit the complete frozen OUKITEL WP9, LATIMERIA 26800 mAh, TG90 6000 mAh, and JUBOTY 7000 mAh listing bodies; reconcile the frozen winter-field, battery-pack, and damage discussions with the low-temperature terminal-voltage, cutoff, insulation, and battery-management mechanisms; recommend one bounded route or defer while preserving every seller, community, compatibility, temperature, and missing-test limitation; and specify a minus 15 degree full-shift preflight for any conditional setup.

accepted_phrases: A lithium-ion equivalent-circuit model separates open-circuit voltage from loaded terminal voltage, includes ohmic resistance and dynamic voltage drops, and says internal resistance increases significantly at low temperature. Cell phones can shut down when cutoff voltage is reached, including while significant capacity remains, and a battery management system may monitor temperature, voltage, state of charge and state of power or reduce and stop operation under an under-temperature boundary. Together these generic mechanisms make a cold load-related voltage collapse and protective cutoff plausible even while the display recently showed about 40 percent. They do not diagnose this phone, establish its exact hidden charge, prove its battery management implementation, or replace device measurements.

Audit the complete frozen product bodies rather than ranking printed capacity or rugged wording. The OUKITEL WP9 body displays $219.99 and 67/100 over 12 reviews, claims 8000 mAh, up to 48 hours, IP68 and an operating range of minus 10 to 70 degrees Celsius, and restricts several major United States carriers. Its stated floor does not include minus 15 degrees Celsius. The LATIMERIA body displays $25.99 and 65/100 over 12 reviews, claims 26800 mAh, IPX4 and a best operating range of minus 20 to 60 degrees Celsius, but calls solar charging emergency-only and says to wall-charge before travel. The TG90 body displays $25.99 and 65/100 over 12 reviews, claims 6000 mAh, pocket dimensions, one USB port and two built-in cables, but states no cold operating range. The JUBOTY body displays $20.83 with no reviews, claims 7000 mAh, states a 0 to 45 degree Celsius working range, and pairs a 150 percent extra-life heading with a sentence claiming 20 percent. Do not treat any frozen product as proven for an uninterrupted minus 15 degree full shift. Keep the current phone with a wall-charged LATIMERIA 26800 mAh bank carried warm in the same insulated inner pouch as the evidence-bounded interim route, but rely on it only after the representative minus 15 load and full-shift preflight passes. LATIMERIA is the only frozen option whose seller-stated range includes minus 15 degrees, yet that is not independent endurance proof and its solar input is emergency-only. Do not replace the phone with OUKITEL on ruggedness or 8000 mAh alone because its stated floor is minus 10 and carrier compatibility is restricted. Do not rely on TG90 because it states no cold range, or JUBOTY because its stated floor is 0 degrees and its runtime wording conflicts. If the preflight cannot be run or fails, defer deployment and obtain independently validated cold-rated equipment rather than inferring success from capacity, seller wording or anecdotes.

Thermal insulation reduces heat transfer but the generic source gives no guaranteed phone-pouch duration. Before a work shift, wall-charge the current phone and LATIMERIA bank indoors, disable reliance on the integrated solar panel, keep the phone and bank together in the intended insulated inner pouch, and reproduce minus 15 degrees Celsius with the representative screen, radio, application and cable load. Record phone and bank temperature, state of charge, elapsed time, shutdown or warning, delivered charge, cable behavior and recovery after warming. Repeat through the required full-shift duration and define pass and abort thresholds for uninterrupted service, safe temperature and successful backup transfer. A seller temperature range, generic insulation principle or cold-field anecdote cannot substitute for this product-specific replay.

A soldier-thread commenter reports two to three phone charges from a medium power bank and at least one from a small bank during a really cold field exercise, while other participants describe long brand use and weak integrated solar. A separate battery-pack thread contrasts portable 10000 mAh packs with heavier 22000 to 23000 mAh packs and includes a 26000 mAh multiple-charge report. A damage thread contains an owner's disputed attribution of an iPhone screen failure to a random pack and warnings that unknown products may misstate protocol, capacity, or speed. These discussions motivate carrying a backup, checking portability, compatibility, labels and safety, and avoiding reliance on integrated solar, but none states the needed minus 15 temperature, controlled load and matching frozen product data.
